function: MIMO symbol detection with a deep-unfolded, momentum-induced projected-gradient-descent network (MomentNet). p. 1
system: Uplink MIMO, (Nr,Nt) = (32,8) and (32,16), QPSK and 16-QAM, perfect CSI at the receiver; no RIS; frequency band not stated. pp. 1, 4
method: Deep unfolding of momentum projected gradient descent with trainable per-layer weights and one momentum parameter; supervised offline training (Adam, 10,000 iterations, batch 512). pp. 3-4
data_channel: Synthetic i.i.d Rayleigh fading; H and x randomly generated at each training iteration; no 3GPP model, public dataset, or measurement. p. 4
test_conditions: Training data and tests come from the same i.i.d Rayleigh model, (Nr,Nt) = (32,8) and (32,16), QPSK and 16-QAM; SNR sweep; no unseen condition. p. 4
baselines: Classical: MMSE, BLAST, SDR, ML bound. Learned: DetNet, ScNet, FS-Net, MMNet, OAMPNet2, VBINet. p. 4
metrics: Symbol error rate versus SNR, layer-wise SER, FLOPs count, SER versus FLOPs, learning curves. pp. 3-5
complexity: FLOPs per layer O(2K^2) (Table I), equal to FS-Net; 2KL+1 trainable parameters; saves 73%, 89%, 98% of FLOPs versus VBINet, MMNet, OAMPNet2. pp. 3-5
q1_support: p. 4: "an i.i.d Rayleigh fading channel"; a custom textbook model, and no 3GPP, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is mentioned.
q2_support: p. 4: "randomly generated for each iteration"; Fig. 4 reports (32,8) and (32,16) separately, and no test on a configuration, channel, or modulation unseen in training, or fine-tuning, is stated.
q3_support: p. 4: "classic linear and nonlinear detectors like MMSE, BLAST, and SDR" and "previously developed DL-detectors [10], [11], [12], [13], [14], [15]", compared on SER in Fig. 4.
q4_support: p. 4: "comparison of the computational cost of each detection algorithm in FLOPs count"; Table I (p. 5) gives O(2K^2) per layer for MomentNet.
q5_support: p. 4: "randomly generated for each iteration"; the data are synthetic, and no code link or public dataset is stated anywhere in the paper.
notes: Deep unfolding with trained parameters counts as learned. The paper says alpha depends on the channel model and is 0.25 for i.i.d Rayleigh (p. 3), but no other channel is tested. Figs. 4 to 7 and Table I were also read on the page images.
